t: Born into the Quraysh of Mecca and orphaned young, Muhammad reported in about 610 that he had received the first of the revelations that Muslims hold to be the word of God, and began preaching publicly in 613.

After 13 years of persecution in Mecca he and his followers migrated to Medina in 622, the event that began the Islamic calendar, and there he led a community that grew through treaties, raids and wars.
By his death on 8 June 632 most of the Arabian Peninsula had converted to Islam, and the dispute over who should succeed him shaped the later division between Sunni and Shia Muslims.
dyk: The Quran contains comparatively little direct information about Muhammad himself, although it names him in several verses and briefly refers to episodes such as the migration to Yathrib and the Battle of Badr.
ev: Muhammad is born in Mecca into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh
He reports a visit from Gabriel in the cave of Hira and the first revelation
The Hijrah: he and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina
The Muslims win the Battle of Badr against a larger Meccan force
The Treaty of Hudaybiyya establishes a ten-year truce with the Quraysh
He marches on Mecca with 10,000 men and takes the city with minimal casualties
He leads the Farewell Pilgrimage and dies in Medina on 8 June

f.born: c. 570 in Mecca, in the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh, son of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Amina bint Wahb
f.died: 8 June 632 in Medina, after an illness of some days; buried where he died, in Aisha's house, later included in the Prophet's Mosque
f.role: Founder of Islam; held by Muslims to be the Seal of the Prophets, the last prophet sent by God; leader of the Muslim community in Medina from 622 and of most of Arabia by 632
f.known: the revelations that form the Quran; the Hijrah to Medina in 622; the Constitution of Medina; the Battle of Badr; the conquest of Mecca; the Farewell Pilgrimage; the sunnah preserved in the hadith
